question: Does a replication from the authors' public data reproduce the published difference-in-differences estimates of Card and Krueger (1994), including their standard errors and the regression sample, and how much of the headline estimate remains when extreme store-level employment changes are winsorized, a check with no published result that we found?
hypotheses: H1 (replication; tolerances fixed now): (a) Table 3, row 3, column (iii): the change in mean FTE employment, NJ minus PA, is within 0.05 of 2.76 and its standard error within 0.05 of 1.36; (b) Table 3, row 4 (balanced sample): within 0.05 of 2.75, SE within 0.05 of 1.34; (c) Table 4, column (i): the regression sample has 357 stores and the New Jersey coefficient is within 0.05 of 2.33 with SE within 0.05 of 1.19. Each part is reported as reproduced or not; the 0.05 tolerance allows for rounding and for differences between data releases (the public files accompany Myth and Measurement, chapter 2, and may not be identical to the AER files).

H2 (robustness check with no published result found): after winsorizing store-level changes in FTE employment at the 5th and 95th percentiles of the pooled distribution, the NJ-minus-PA difference keeps the same sign and at least half the magnitude of the replicated headline estimate. This is judged on the point estimate, not on significance: with one treated and one control state, conventional inference is unreliable (Conley and Taber 2011).
contribution: An independent, fully logged replication of a canonical difference-in-differences estimate from the authors' public data that also targets the published standard errors and the 357-store regression sample, which an earlier informal replication did not reproduce; plus one robustness check chosen without a published result to aim at. The crew had read the published results of other robustness checks; what the process rules out is specification search within this study.

tasks.title: The published estimates and definitions; later critiques and robustness checks (e.g. Neumark-Wascher payroll data, Card-Krueger 2000 reply)
